content.title: Urgent Graco car seat recall because of ‘structural issue’: What parents need to know
content.text: NewsGraco has recalled 5,126 certain SnugRide Turn & Slide and Modes Nest Travel Systems with Snugride Turn & Slide infant child seats because they may detach from the base during a crash.GracoBy Deb Kiner | dkiner@pennlive.comGraco has recalled 5,126 infant car seats because the seat may detach from the base during a crash.The company recalled certain SnugRide Turn & Slide and Modes Nest Travel Systems with SnugRide Turn & Slide infant seats sold from January 2026 through March 2026 at Amazon, Babylist, Target, Walmart and on gracobaby.com.Graco said the recall was triggered by “a structural issue identified during a post-production laboratory test.”“We know parents rely on Graco products every day, and we understand this may create frustration and disruption for families. We are working quickly to support affected families and will provide a replacement product at no cost,” Graco said.The affected model numbers are as follows:Infant car seats2231809 (noir/black)2231887 (sandstone/tan)2231806 (mulberry/girl-plum)2231885 (sandstone/tan)2231881 (noir/black)2231884 (noir/black)Car seat base2231810 (black)Travel system2243083 (noir/black)Owners should immediately stop using the car seat attached to the base. The seat should be used without the base until a replacement is received.No other Graco rotating car seats are affected, including EasyTurn and Turn2Me. No other SnugRide models are affected.Owners can register for the recall online at recalls.gracobaby.com.Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed this month. For more information, call Graco customer service at 800-345-4109.This mini trampoline sold at Walmart is recalled after a frightening injury This gaming PC component is missing a crucial warning that could save your lifeWhy you should immediately remove two pieces from this pet vet toy your child might ownNovelty finger lights sold at discount stores pulled from shelves over battery hazardWireless phone chargers recalled again after explosions, death of woman Deb Kiner has worked at PennLive.com/The Patriot-News since 1987 having served in a variety of positions including reporter, copy editor and editor.
